verdicts.reasoning: Three samples actually put a tiled figure on screen (GridArea at seeds 23, 103 and 127) and the question cannot be answered without reading the shaded array of unit squares, so the area-as-tiled-array picture is present in the set. The pupil reads a supplied illustration rather than constructing one — that is the ceiling of what these samples demonstrate.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: In all three visual items rows/cols is smaller than grid_size (2x2 inside grid_size [3,3] at seed 23; 3x3 inside [4,4] at seed 103; 2x3 inside [3,4] at seed 127). If the drawn canvas shows the full grid_size, the stem's 'Look at the 2x2 array' names something smaller than what is drawn, and a pupil counting every drawn cell at seed 23 would get 9 rather than the keyed 4.

verdicts.reasoning: The estimating frame is explicit in seven samples: 'Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all' at seeds 42, 57, 78 and 118, and 'About how many tiles in total will you use?' at seeds 11 and 91.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: Every key is the exact row-by-column product (2 rows x 7 columns keys 14 at seed 42) and the distractors are not near-misses that an approximation would separate, so 'estimate' functions as wording over an exact tiling count. That may be the intended grade-3 reading, but nothing here rewards approximating rather than computing.

verdicts.reasoning: What is asked for is the total covering of the figure — seed 57's 6 rows and 4 columns 'covered edge-to-edge' keys 24 — which is the area expressed as a tile count, and the same quantity is behind the shaded-square counts at seed 127.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: The word 'area' itself never appears in any stem in this set; the quantity is always phrased as a number of tiles or shaded squares.

verdicts.reasoning: Squares turn up as the covered figure with equal row and column counts: seed 11 fits 5 rows and 5 columns over a square, seed 64 tiles a 2x2 square, and seed 23's payload types the shape as 'square'.

Genuinely unequal side counts appear several times over — 2 by 7 at seed 42, 6 by 4 at seed 57, 7 by 3 at seed 91 — and seed 127 carries shape_type 'rectangle' on a 2x3 grid, so rectangles are not just squares relabelled.

The covering unit is named in the stems as a square tile: 'laying unit square tiles' at seeds 11 and 91, 'covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles' at seed 42, with the edge-to-edge phrasing ruling out gaps and overlaps.

The answer is denominated in tiles rather than in a length or a labelled measure — seed 91 keys 21 for 7 rows by 3 columns and seed 78 keys 8 for 4 rows by 2 columns — so the tile is the unit of the result, not just a prop in the story.
